reviewType: Internal qualitative comparison with actual photographs and scoped authoritative biology; not independent biological validation
humanFindings: The public0.6.47model remained too deep-bodied, with an abrupt navy/white belly scheme and overly conspicuous appendages. The user identified these appearance failures; its initial software checks were not evidence of realistic biological accuracy.
The source dorsal fin was too far forward for the selected blue-whale exterior. The posterior joined surface now carries the smaller fin farther aft.
changes: v0.6.48: Selected elongated/slender scene aspect (longitudinal 1.22, depth 0.80) applied to body and rig together; lower dorsal-fin exterior carried farther aft on a smooth monotone joined posterior rest-surface, flatter rostrum and more compact pectoral envelope. Two posed-space subdivision passes with inverse-skin rebinding retain continuous skin and interpolated UV/weights. A reproducible 2.2-pixel smoothed atlas with a 24-pixel broad field separates bounded local luminance detail from the earlier abrupt navy/white scheme, recolouring the whole surface grey-blue. This is authored pigment, not photographic sampling or calibrated optics. Original binary prefix, nodes/skins/accessors and animation samples are retained; two other active images unchanged. Regional rest-surface/rig relations remain unmeasured; the original clip is not fitted biomechanics. Legacy0.6.47delivery remains exactly reproducible using legacy-v0647.

sourceLimits: Naturalis describes bluish-grey dorsal and somewhat lighter ventral surfaces with variable mottling. Selected NOAA indexed field text allows white, grey or yellowish bellies; the new grey-blue choice is not a claim that all white ventral colour is impossible.
The same grey-blue palette persists through every action. Its numerical colour mapping is authored, not reflectance measured from the water-filtered photographs.

Six alternative artist metadata/preview thumbnails were actually inspected. None became a new downloaded/reviewed GLB or a scientifically validated replacement. Titles alone are not exact-species identity proof.

The actual new source-linked3072x2048Flickr original was downloaded and inspected. The current2600x1800Commons file is a crop; the report uses the whole Flickr frame. Creator credit is NOAA Photo Library; no named individual photographer is supplied in the inspected source.
The existing Gough2019text/methods/Table1access scope remains unchanged. No new source video, fitted motion, calibrated physiology or research-figure inspection is claimed.
remaining: Proportions, fin dimensions and grey-blue colour mapping are authored qualitative choices, not measurements or a specimen fit.

Skin mottling remains a locally normalized and recoloured artist atlas. Natural individual variation, underwater scattering, scars, epibionts, wet specular response and deep tissue optics are not reconstructed.
Source animation is a finite local fluke/flipper excerpt, not measured full swimming, respiration, feeding, flow, contact force, energetics or physiology.
Mouth/baleen, ventral pouch/pleat depth, paired blowhole rims and eye anatomy remain simplified.
Final software compatibility views cannot establish working WebGL material/normal-map optics.
The caudal/back slope and local rig-bend crease, frontal cross-section, fluke thickness and fin profile remain selected artist geometry rather than fitted living soft tissue.
